Disputes that are not resolved at the institutional-level will be referred to the Interinstitutional Articulation/Transfer Committee.

Manhattan Institute is now issuing templates for dismantling DEI educational initiatives in every state across the country WHEREAS Florida is at the forefront of a nationwide campaign to silence Black voices and erase the full and accurate history and contemporary experiences of Black people WHEREAS Florida College System presidents issued a collective statement affirming their view that some diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives are harmful to higher education WHEREAS Governor DeSantis has explicitly stated his aim to defund and dismantle DEI initiatives as well as the governing body and administrative leadership of The New College, a public institution WHEREAS Governor DeSantis and the Florida House of Representatives made demands in January for information regarding the funding of programs related to diversity, equity, inclusion, and critical race theory at colleges and universities, now intending to bar funding for these programs across the higher education system is forbidden, disparagement of these theories is openly allowed and transgressions can be penalized through revoking millions of dollars in state funding WHEREAS public universities and colleges in Florida must nevertheless administer ideological surveys to all higher ed students, faculty and staff, the results of which may be used to drive budgetary decisions WHEREAS students in Florida are nevertheless permitted to seek permission for recording lectures, which may be used in disciplinary or legal actions against faculty WHEREAS all syllabi and reading lists must nevertheless be posted BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that this statement confirms URI's current statement of Foundational Values in espousing a commitment to freedom to learn, teach, create, and conduct research with integrity in the pursuit and dissemination of new knowledge aimed at contributing to the public good, as well as an inclusive, accessible, equitable and diverse community whereby we respect the rights and dignity of all.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that in issuing this statement of support, the University of Rhode Island aspires to serve as a national model for the role a flagship public research university can play in driving transformative change for the betterment of its state and the global human condition.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that this statement applauds the URI Board of Trustees' affirmation of the university's determination to embrace Rhode Island ’s heritage of independent thought, valuing creativity and scholarship, diversity, fairness, and respect, engaged learning and civic involvement, and intellectual and ethical leadership.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that this statement affirms our commitment to the ideals of the URI Office of Community, Equity and Diversity and its core values of advancing equity, inclusion, and diversity in the global community and modeling honesty, integrity, and social justice.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that this statement explicitly stands by the URI Cornerstones, acknowledging the University of Rhode Island as a principled community guided by values, including the principles of independent choice, intellectual curiosity, open-mindedness, free expression, the rights and dignity of each individual and group, working to understand and respect differences, and the rejection of prejudice, discrimination, and intolerance.

Existing Language 8.59.10 Assessment of student learning outcomes shall be coordinated by the Learning Outcomes Oversight Committee (LOOC; see 5.84.10 – 5.84.13) in cooperation with the Assistant Director of Student Learning, Outcomes Assessment and Accreditation (see 2.22.21).
The following policies shall apply to this process: 8.59.11 Academic Program Engagement.

All undergraduate, professional, and graduate academic programs, including General Education, shall be actively engaged in student learning outcomes assessment as evidenced by, but not limited to: a) Published student learning outcomes that are clear statements of what students are expected to gain, achieve, demonstrate, or know at the completion of the academic program.
These student learning outcomes shall be published on the program’s website as well as on the website for the Office of Student Learning, Outcomes Assessment, and Accreditation (SLOAA).
These student learning outcomes shall be periodically reviewed by the academic program for ongoing relevance. b) A plan of student learning outcomes assessment that is endorsed by the program’s faculty.
Plans should include a regular and predictable cycle for collecting and analyzing assessment data, for discussing curricular and programmatic changes, for implementing interventions, and for re-assessing the impact of implemented changes.

Outcomes assessment plans will be published on each program’s website as well as on the SLOAA website. c) Reports of student learning outcomes assessment that are provided to SLOAA using staggered cycles of no more than 3 years.
